On the one hand, the proposed method introduces a scalable and versatile technique that can be seamlessly integrated with existing local contrast measure detection methods, on the other hand, it effectively enhances the background suppression capability of detection methods that utilize multiscale strategies. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the existing maximization multiscale method in suppressing background clutter.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Legal Practice: Enhancing Case Prediction and Legal Research
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Legal case prediction (LCP) and decision assistance strive to allow systems to forecast the outcome of legal cases after comprehending an explanation of the evidence, using artificial intelligence (AI) in legal practices. This work offers an enhanced supervision-based LCP framework that accounts for the consecutive dependency of every sub-task in the LCP activity. The empirical outcomes confirm the efficiency of the conceptual paradigm and the procedure surveillance process used in this structure. Initially, textual characteristics were extracted using the convolutional neural network (CNN) technique, and then data characteristics were reduced in size using the principal component assessment method. The predictive paradigm built around supervision analysis is then presented initially. When simulating the dependent connection between consecutive sub-data collections, supervision analysis is used to assure the accuracy of the acquired dependent data, while a genetic algorithm is used to maximize the variables and enhance the final case prediction efficiency. When evaluated with the standard approach, the proposed method produced outstanding outcomes on 4 separate publicly accessible legal databases. The implementation of autonomous LCP can not just help lawyers, attorneys, and other specialists make more effective legal decisions, but it additionally offers legal assistance to persons who lack legal understanding.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Detection with Severity Identification Using K-Means Clustering
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: In the current investigation, we present a methodological framework that utilizes k-means clustering for the identification and measurement of cerebral neoplasms. The principal aim is to precisely as certain the existence of tumors within MRI scans and to evaluate the percentage of tumor involvement within the cerebral tissue. The proposed methodology initiates with the preprocessing of MRI images to enhance contrast and mitigate noise, thus augmenting the efficacy of subsequent analytical processes. Thereafter, k-means clustering is utilized to partition the MRI images into discrete clusters, with each cluster representing various tissue types within the brain. By leveraging the intrinsic intensity disparities between healthy and tumor-afflicted tissues, it becomes feasible to discern the clusters pertaining to tumor tissues. Subsequent to the segmentation phase, advanced post-processing techniques are implemented to refine the segmentation outcomes and extract significant features that are indicative of tumor presence and extent. These features encompass the dimensions, morphology, and spatial distribution of tumor regions within the MRI scans. Through a comprehensive quantitative analysis of these features, it is possible to estimate the percentage of tumor involvement in the brain, thereby furnishing invaluable insights for medical practitioners. Utilizing a dataset of brain MRI scans that encompasses both tumorous and healthy instances, the efficacy of the proposed methodology is evaluated. Furthermore, the estimated percentage of tumor involvement is juxtaposed against the ground truth annotations provided by medical professionals to authenticate the quantitative analysis. Overall, the suggested methodology demonstrates favorable results in the identification and quantification of cerebral tumors via the utilization of k-means clustering. By providing accurate assessments of tumor presence and the extent of involvement, the proposed technique possesses the capacity to assist medical practitioners in making well-informed choices regarding patient diagnosis and therapeutic approaches, ultimately improving patient outcomes and the overall standard of healthcare.

articleTitle: Ensuring Data Integrity in Multi-Tenant Cloud Environments Through Advanced Testing
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: fortunately, multi-tenant cloud environments offer a more cost-effective provisioning model that consumes infrastructure to store and access data. As the volume of sensitive data processed and stored in the cloud continues to grow, ensuring data integrity has become a top concern for organizations. Data integrity is the information that is correct, consistent, and reliable is stored in the cloud. To address this issue, we also present a solution that allows us to maintain integrity in a multi-tenant cloud environment using advanced testing. The standard approach to testing (functional and performance testing) does not identify and will enable us to prevent data integrity problems. That's because these approaches describe the system's functionality and performance rather than the accuracy of the system's data. They proposed a solution that used techniques like anomaly detection, data profiling, and data quality checks to discover possible integrity issues in the dataset. The new techniques work within the testing process, while all data is assessed for integrity before being stored in the cloud.

articleTitle: Metamaterial-Loaded Circular Patch Antenna for UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The paper presents a circular patch antenna loaded with a double circular split ring resonator designed for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) applications. Here the coaxial probe feed excites the patch antenna. Coaxial probe feed has low spurious radiation when compared to other feeding mechanisms. The antenna offers a bandwidth of 2.37 to 2.43 GHz, which is suitable for UAV applications. The parametric study involves changing the ground plane's dimension, varying the substrate's thickness, and adding a split ring resonator structure. The metamaterial-based patch antenna achieves a gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10.4 \mathbf{dBi}$</tex> and omnidirectional radiation patterns at a resonant frequency of 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Evaluation of RISC-V Embedded Processor Using HDL
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Today's world has seen the dawn of a new era with a sudden spike of interest much towards generative AI and Machine Learning throughout the globe and with computational powers beginning to show their might, we need fast and efficient microprocessors. To achieve higher efficiency, modern processors often adopt the RISC (Reduced Instruction Set Computer) design principle, which emphasizes a smaller and simpler set of instructions, each executive in a uniform amount of time. In this research, we have tried to deploy a 5-stage pipelined general-purpose microprocessor architecture that achieves a clock period of 0.59 nanoseconds, translating to an operational frequency of 1.69 GHz through the implementation of optimization techniques in Verilog code. Additionally, the use of True Single- Phase Clocking (TSPC) flip-flops reduce the transistor count per flip-flop by approximately 50%, leading to a 20% decrease in overall power consumption. This paper highlights the application of RISC-V embedded processor design in obtaining a n-stage pipelined architecture for a general-purpose microprocessor using Verilog HDL on ModelSim and Xilinx.

articleTitle: Spectrum Sensing Methodology Using Artificial Intelligence for Cognitive Radio Network
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Spectrum sensing is an essential part of cognitive radio networks (CRNs) that enables efficient utilisation of the radio frequency spectrum and dynamic spectrum access. Conventional spectrum sensing technologies, such as energy detection, matched filtering, and cyclostationary features recognition, are often computationally complex, noise-sensitive, and unable to detect signals at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches have become a viable substitute to deal with these issues. CRNs can provide more precise, flexible, and effective spectrum sensing owing to AI approaches. In intricate and dynamic situations, these algorithms can identify primary users, predict spectrum usage, and categorise spectrum accessibility. Major AI-driven techniques for spectrum sensing are reviewed in this work, with an emphasis on supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning techniques. The suggested approach supports the creation of intelligent, independent CRNs for next-generation wireless networks by improving spectrum efficacy, cutting down on sensing time, and facilitating real-time decision-making.

articleTitle: Conventional and Intelligent Control Schemes for Handling A Helicopter's Pitch Axis
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: In this paper, a comparative study of conventional LQR controller, optimized PID controller and intelligent Fuzzy logic controller is demonstrated while achieving the desired pitch axis trajectories of a 2-DOF helicopter system. During this process, TLBO optimized PID controller is used to track down the trajectory angle of pitch axis of helicopter system and this performance is compared with inference rules of fuzzy system and a conventional LQR controller. The membership function parameters, exploration - exploitation scheme of optimization algorithm are discussed while addressing the problem of trajectory tracking. The parameter tuning and stable response of pitch axis of helicopter model is achieved on MATLAB/Simulink platform, on which the comparison is accomplished through time response analysis.

articleTitle: Semi-Supervised Deep Learning Based Method for Abnormality Detection in Videos
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Anomaly detection refers to recognition of events different from normal ones for example road accident, fight, robbery, arsenal etc. Anomaly identification in real world surveillance videos is an important application of computer vision. The work proposed in the paper detects anomalous events in surveillance videos dataset and is based upon semi supervised deep learning model. We trained the model using UCF Crime dataset that consists of 950 normal videos and 950 anomalous videos. The anomaly videos in the dataset consists of 13 different types of anomalies such as Abuse, arrest, explosion, fight etc. that generally occur in real life. The anomaly in the dataset is labelled at video level and not at a specific frame in a video to define the semi supervised nature of learning paradigm. The extracted 3D features from dataset are fed into the multilayered deep learning model. Experimental results show that our approach has significant improvement over state-of-the-art approaches for anomaly detection in surveillance videos. The accuracy of model comes out to be 83.96 percent, that is improvement over other methods.

articleTitle: Detection of Quality Deep Fake Images and Videos Using Customised Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Due to advancements in artificial intelligence there are numerous deep fake images and video collections are available on the Internet and social media. The primary aim of the study is to analyse the deep fake images and videos since the quality is constantly improving a novel method was developed for accurate detection of quality deep fakes. The suggested approach uses a customised convolutional neural network (CNN) technique that uses facial landmark detection to extract structured data from photos and video frames before feeding it into the methods of CNN. The customised CNN model is augment-based CNN for generation of fake images and fake data. Involves about 260 films from the data set in which 202 images are made up while others were real images. About 300 videos are used in which 250 videos are fake and 50 were real the proposed model achieved the accuracy of 95.58% and 0.97 AUC score that outperforms the existing models like MLP-CNN and CNN. Additionally, the method succeeds with greater accuracy then the conventional models like DST -Net, VGG 16 Efficient Net. This research study's primary goal is to create a new CNN learning method for identifying high-quality deep fake photos and videos.

articleTitle: Enhancing Performance through the Integration of LSTM and ARCH Model for Monitoring and Predicting Air Pollution
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Any chemical, physical, or biological substance that changes the way the air normally works is called an air pollutant. Either indoors or outside, air pollution is possible. Significantly harmful pollutants to human health include particulates, ozone, carbon monoxide, nitrogen dioxide, and sulphur dioxide. Environmental and indoor air pollution, a major source of illness and death, is a factor in respiratory and other disorders. LSTM networks are well adapted to categorising, analysing, and forecasting results from analyses of time series as there may be unanticipated lags between major events in time sequences. A model for a time series variance is known as an ARCH (auto-regressive conditionally heteroscedastic) model. It is possible to characterise a fluctuating, potentially unpredictable variance using ARCH models. The majority of the time, an ARCH model is utilised in circumstances where there may be brief spikes in variation, even if it could theoretically be used to explain a variance that increases continuously over time. The goal of this project is to create a novel hybrid forecasting model that employs a feature selection method utilising the ARCH algorithm and a long-short-term memory neural network (LSTM). A consequence of careless human action is poor air quality and climate variability. Many respiratory disorders are brought on by PM2.5, which penetrates the lungs and heart. To safeguard the ecosystem and all of its inhabitants, including human beings, development in air quality prediction is essential.

articleTitle: GRU Based Autoencoder with Maximum Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transfrmers for Brain Tumor Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: A new approach based on autoencoder with GRU (gated recurrent unit) and discrete transforms for multi scale features of MRI images. Most of the systems fail to adequately handle sequentially dependencies or effectively leverage multi resolution scale. Therefore, in this paper we are analyzing a spatial and temporal features of brain tumor MRI images by imposing modified wavelet transforms for multi-scale analysis with a sequential modeling approach. Masoud Nickparver's Kaggle is used to train and test this model. In this study, 80% of the data are used for training and 20% of the data is used for testing. The implementation outputs give strong validation by achieving 98.88% classification accuracy for four classes. The F1 score and Precision of our novel framework are 98% and 98.30% respectively.

articleTitle: Smart Attendance Management System Using Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Managing attendance in educational institutions is often a time-consuming and error-prone task, with traditional methods like roll calls or sign-in sheets being inefficient and susceptible to proxy attendance. This paper presents a Smart Attendance Management System that leverages facial recognition technology to automate the attendance process. By using cameras to capture images of students, the system recognizes their faces and marks their attendance in real time. Developed in Python, the system employs the K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithm for accurate face recognition. Once attendance is recorded, it is stored in a CSV file and can be visualized using the flask web application. The proposed system significantly reduces manual effort, ensures accuracy, and operates efficiently in real-time environments.

articleTitle: Sustainable Civil Engineering Practices: Implementing Green Building Technologies with AI Assistance
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Due to its substantial energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, and resource depletion, the construction sector is one of the biggest causes of environmental deterioration. Sustainable building techniques have become a vital strategy for mitigating these issues and lowering the environmental impact of civil engineering projects. Green buildings are ones that preserve or enhance the local standard of living via the use of sustainable construction techniques. Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Green Construction is used to analyse data collected from monitoring the construction site and utilising predictive analytics to make decisions that impact a project's quality, safety, profitability, and timeline. The goal of the planned study was to assess the potential for AI in Green Building Construction (AI-GBC) to lower utility costs and carbon emissions. RF and GA are used by artificial intelligence to lower carbon dioxide emissions and energy consumption. The accuracy of the AI-GBC is assessed using a number of statistical measures, including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), and Root Mean Squared Log Error (RMSLE). With prediction accuracies over 96%, both Machine Learning (ML) models produced favourable outcomes. With an R2 of 0.96, GA models performed rather well in terms of predicting Co_2. 98% will undertake a k-fold cross-validation analysis, and 96% will finish a performance analysis. In order to avoid overfitting and guarantee the accuracy of the results obtained from the extended modelling technique, cross-validation is employed.

articleTitle: Managing AI-Driven Innovations: Aligning Technological Advancements with Strategic Business Objectives
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing company strategy at a rapid pace, making it necessary to connect organizational goals with technology innovation. With a focus on machine learning model evaluation, this research investigates AI-driven innovations and how they might be incorporated into strategic decision-making. Several models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, and Neural Networks, are examined to determine key performance measures comprising accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, RMSE, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The findings demonstrate the trade-offs amongst model robustness, accuracy, training time, and intricacy in a variety of scenarios, including noisy and unbalanced data. To inform AI-driven business decisions, feature significance and efficiency on huge datasets are being investigated. Organizations can maximize AI adoption, improve operational efficiency, and keep a competitive edge by utilizing machine learning evaluation methods. This research emphasizes how crucial it is to match AI capabilities with business plans to guarantee efficient implementation and value creation from technological advancements.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven QoS Prediction in 6G Networks Under $\alpha-\eta-\mu$ Fading with Selection Combining and Co-Channel Interference Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: In this paper, we study machine learning for resource utilization and QoS performance improvement in 6G networks under <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha-\eta-\mu$</tex> fading and co-channel interference (CCI). We conduct extensive experiments in simulation comparing our proposal with previous work and showing substantial improvements for both throughput, latency and resource efficiency over traditional as well as deep reinforcement learning based approaches. Their adaptive nature enables real-time optimization, and they run well in both dynamic and complex network conditions. Our experimental results illustrate that machine learned models significantly outperform state-of-the-art baselines on the following dimensions prediction accuracy, resource management and QoS metrics. This work underscores the importance of machine learning as a core enabler for sustainable 6G networks and providing better performance in future wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Prediction of Heart Disease Using ML Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: There are a variety of approaches utilised in the processing of healthcare data. Data mining is utilised quite frequently. The majority of deaths are caused by cardiovascular disorders. It is a risk factor for heart disease. The proportions of risk factors for heart disease can be computed using this technique. Data sources can be categorised based on healthcare factors. Using a data mining classification approach, this system does analysis on such parameters. The datasets are analysed using the Decision Tree Algorithm and the Naive Bayes Algorithm, both of which are written in Python. The Decision Tree Algorithm has the highest precision for heart disease. Introduction

articleTitle: Blockchain-Enabled Financial Reengineering for Sustainable Social Innovation in the Indian IT Industry
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Blockchain enabled financial system enhance the efficiency, security and transparency. The study examines the sustainable social innovation in the Indian IT industry. It leverages the decentralized nature of blockchain so that the organizations streamline the financial operations, enhance accountability and reduce fraud to foster economic growth. The study examines the applications of blockchain including secure digital payments, decentralized finance and smart contracts and the impact on initiatives for corporate sustainability. The challenges are highlighted in the study including adoption hurdles, scalability and regulatory barriers. The findings suggest development of business model with social responsibility to promote long-term sustainability in Indian IT sector.

articleTitle: Effective Energy Efficiency Methods for Distribution Transformers
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: In this paper, three different energy efficiency schemes have been studied for the different ratings of distribution transformers. The schemes used for calculating the efficiency are single-point efficiency methods (SPEM), Multi-point efficiency method (MPEM), and Dual criteria method (DCM). The objectives of these schemes are mainly used to calculate the efficiency at various loading levels and provide a better variation of designs for the selection of transformers as per the needs of the manufacturers and customers. A simulation study has been carried out to demonstrate the effectiveness of the applied schemes. A comparative analysis among the schemes has been done in terms of efficiencies at several loading levels as per schemes which help the manufacturers to select the optimal design criteria and differentiate the design alternatives at specific loading levels.

articleTitle: Technological Advancement of Big Data Analytics in Enhancing Financial Decision-Making and Trade Performance in Emerging Markets
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The revolutionary potential of big data analytics (BDA) is causing a dramatic transformation in the field of financial risk management (FRM). Financial companies are now leveraging massive databases as more than just historical information to change risk management practices. The financial industry has seen a paradigm shift as a result of machine learning's (ML) convergence, which has enabled businesses to gain deeper insights and make well-informed decisions. This abstract examines the various connections between these developments and demonstrates their effects on risk management, financial operations, predictive analytics, and customer-focused services. Proactive risk assessment, accurate forecast models, and customised financial plans are made possible by the integration of large databases and complex technologies. It has problems with interpretability, data privacy, and ethical use even though it is revolutionising the sector. The transformational potential and related ramifications of ML in the financial arena are examined in this paper.

articleTitle: Generate Topics and Filter Novelties at Scale with Pre-Trained Language Models: A GPT-2 Method
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The exponential rise of digital material calls for the development of more sophisticated approaches to the formation of topics that guarantee semantic richness, diversity, and scalability within the content. This research introduces an innovative pipeline employing the pre-trained Generative Pre-trained Transformer 2 (GPT-2) model to tackle issues related to topic coherence, redundancy, and the effective processing of extensive textual datasets to integrates text segmentation, novelty filtration, and semantic coherence enhancement. Text chunking facilitates the processing of extensive datasets by partitioning information into manageable chunks, whereas novelty filtering utilizes Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) vectorization and cosine similarity measures to remove redundancy. Experiments on a news dataset illustrated the pipeline's efficacy, with filtered GPT-2 outputs attaining higher coherence scores (0.85) than raw GPT-2 (0.75) and conventional approaches such as Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) (0.45). Chunking was essential for sustaining scalability, with an ideal size of 800 tokens achieving a compromise between computational efficiency and precision. The methodology substantially surpassed traditional methodologies in producing distinctive, contextually relevant themes, rendering it appropriate for applications including content analysis, document organization, and knowledge discovery. Future endeavors will concentrate on optimizing for domain-specific datasets, multilingual applications, and minimizing computational overhead to improve adaptability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Wavelet Tree Approach for Searching and Indexing in Geographical Information Retrieval
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Spatial data in Geographical Information Retrieval (GIR) plays an increasingly important role in applications such as spatial planning, crisis management or context-based services. Spatial data makes an already difficult task even more difficult for traditional indexing methods to perform. They are not created with the idea of these complex dimensions built in and need to be more efficient and practical regarding search and retrieval processes. In this paper, we discussa data structure, a wavelet tree-based system named WaveGIR, that supports searching through summarizations by taking advantage of wavelet transform in the multiresolution property. The wavelet tree structure consumes spatial data in a compressed way and permits fast access and retrieval of geographic information. We compare our approach against standard indexing mechanisms on various datasets regarding query response time, memory utilization and retrieval accuracy. The findings showed notable gains in efficiency and scalability, thereby branding the wavelet tree method as an attractive solution for today's GIR scenarios.

articleTitle: Fraud Detection and Prevention in E-Commerce: Machine Learning Approaches to Secure Transactions
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: E-commerce has grown as a leading marketplace for world trade, but this market has been contaminated by new risks like fraud. Some of the past techniques of detecting fraud do not do well in handling new methods of fraud in the market. The purpose of this research is to understand the offers of the ML approaches for increasing the efficiency of the fraud detection and prevention in e-Commerce processer. This study shows the utility of using different types of the ML solution alone and in comparison, to one another for real-time cyber fraud identification by demonstrating how and why their false positives and overall effectiveness are lower than other methods, as well as how the models adapt to new tactics. Issues like quality of data used, bias in either selection or process of the algorithm are also covered.

articleTitle: Assessment of Germanium-GNR Based Hetero Structured Tunnel Field Effect Transistor for Modulated Work Function
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: This research primarily aimed to investigate the electrostatic behavior of the graphene nanoribbon tunnel field effect transistor (GeGNRTFET). A heterostructured TFET device based on GNR is proposed, utilizing lower bandgap germanium as the source material. This approach, aided by a TCAD simulator, aims to attain a reduced bandgap and enhanced carrier mobility, thereby optimizing the electrical performance. The transfer characteristic of the suggested structure is shown, and many FOMs are then extracted from it. Within this framework, the DC characteristics under examination include the ON current (Ion), transconductance (gm), subthreshold swing (SS), threshold voltage (Vth), and the Ion/Ioff ratio. Images depicting the energy diagrams in both their inactive and active states are also readily accessible. Various values of the gate work function are employed to conduct the research. This research aims to analyze and compare the direct current parameter performance of various tunneling field-effect transistor architectures utilizing diverse source materials. The proposed device demonstrates exceptional performance and substantiates its applicability in low power instances.

articleTitle: Development of Digital Telecommunication to Analyse and Store Complex Media Data: A Way to Data Engineering
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: In the era of digital world data flows are saturated with development of universal multifunctional system to solve problems and to optimise the computing resources. The information system is highly loaded with modern data and large number of resources. articleTitle: High-Frequency Stock Market Price Prediction Using Blockchain and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Researchers and financiers utilize statistics on stock market operation, including past returns, share values, accessible, large, poor, near, and transaction size, to identify trends in stock activity. Technological evaluation can provide financiers with contradictory indications. They focused on predicting the return and risk levels of stock market prices. As a result, the stock market requires an automatic technology that can anticipate the return rate of bitcoin. Deep learning (DL) technology can estimate share market trends employing technological evaluation. This research creates a deep learning-based smart return rate estimation method for blockchain-based stock market prices (RRE-DLBSP). The proposed RRE-DLBSP framework develops an LSTM (long short-term memory) paradigm for RRE assessment. Additionally, the LSTM algorithm's hyperparameters are effectively adjusted using the Adam optimization algorithm, improving prediction efficiency. The Ethereum return rate is selected as the goal and the model outcomes are examined in various ways to ensure the highest functioning of the RRE-DLBSP paradigm. The research results demonstrated the RRE-DLBSP method's superiority over the cutting-edge approaches based on a variety of performance metrics. articleTitle: Evaluating the Efficacy of Deep Learning Models in Identifying and Mitigating Cybersecurity Threats and Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Due to rapid advancement in digital infrastructure and Internet cyber security threats increased in sophisticated way that necessitate advanced strategies for identification and mitigation. The present study uses deep learning models that act as powerful tool for identifying and mitigating cyber security threats and attacks that leverages the capability for detection of complex patterns using large datasets. The Efficacy of the deep learning model can be evaluated using the study for identification of different types of cyber security threats such as DoS, DDoS, ransomware, password hacking and information threat. The proposed model identifies and mitigates the threat in less time and it was tested with two different data sets BoT and ToN. The study explores the model interpretability and robustness for understanding the potentiality and implications based on cyber security solutions. Study findings shows that the proposed model shows highest accuracy of 99.9% and it is comparatively higher than other existing models in identification and mitigation of threats and attacks.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Electronic-Human Resource Management: Transforming Recruitment and Employee Engagement
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The growth of global company activities pushes companies to diversify their activities and encourages human resource management (HRM) to make certain qualified candidates are recruited and staff retained. As a result, businesses have been finding it difficult to assign competent individuals to pertinent positions and offer sufficient training. This research used technological advances to address these issues by employing an electronic-based platform to link the procedures, collect data from candidates employing an electronic-based connection, and match them with relevant work. Initially, the suggested framework demonstrated an integrated approach of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) Cloud E-HRM System by identifying unique characteristics and predicting the applicant's capability beneath different categorization activities. Various programs for creating databases and websites, such as those for image editing, were employed in this research. Even though each methodology had identical accuracy, the CNN-LSTM method outperformed conventional approaches with 91 percent sensitivity and 92 percent accuracy. This CNN-LSTM algorithm helps businesses streamline and improve the hiring procedure by autonomously estimating an employment applicant's appropriateness and projecting his or her employment.

articleTitle: Technological Innovations in Human Resource Management: Using Cloud-Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Utilizing cloud-edge technological advances offers substantial opportunities for resource administration, effectiveness, and financial savings. These characteristics have promoted consumer and enterprise usage of the smart integrated cloud-edge model in the Internet of Things (IoT). In integrated cloud-edge computation, among the major difficulties is human resource management (HRM). Choosing the best capabilities depending on Quality of Service (QoS) considerations is a crucial and significant problem in IoT settings as software and hardware assets in the edge context are allotted for reacting to human demands. In the sense that system effectiveness rises and reaction duration falls with appropriate resource choosing, allotment, and surveillance, HRM may be viewed as an NP issue. articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Architectures for Distributed Big Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: It has created challenges in the processing of data and analysis, which need to go beyond the traditional centralized architecture to solve the current data volume, speed, and types. To address these challenges, fault-tolerant architectures have become one of the keys to meeting the needs of distributed big data analytics. Failure is a normal part of systems; these architectures are meant to accommodate failures of individual components so that the entire system does not need to stop working or, worse, give false results. They make use of several nodes to operate and retain data in a distributed fashion, which supplies excessive scalability and fault tolerance. This means that even if some nodes fail, a fault-tolerant architecture can still provide redundancy by replicating data across many nodes, giving the system redundancy. Fault-tolerant architectures also utilize efficient data processing techniques like partitioning and data parallel processing, to achieve high performance. This allows real-time and near-real-time analysis of streaming data.

articleTitle: Real-Time Emotion Detection in AR Mental Health Applications Using Sentiment Analysis Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) has become an efficient approach in helping various mental health challenges in real-time emotion recognition as well as offering functional therapeutic innovations. This paper provides a conceptual framework that aims to use complex sentiment analysis algorithms and methodological approaches for multichannel emotional state”s classification based on facial expressions, voice, and text. Optimized to run on limited-vendor AR devices, it consists of reduced data preprocessing and customized algorithmic features, all of which allow latency of not more than 50 ms per inference. Extensive experimental evaluations on benchmark datasets illustrate that the proposed approach achieves an average accuracy of 92% in classified primary emotions including happiness, sadness, anger, and neutrality outcomping the state of the art. As the experiments point out, there is a substantial improvement in the perception of multifaceted emotional states due to the integration of multiple modalities. These outcomes confirm the strength and flexibility of the framework, highlighting the fact it also works well in simulated environments and real-world conditions. However, the proposed solution increases user engagement and the overall effectiveness of mental health interventions and support through adaptive and emotional interaction. This research significantly expands the field of digital mental health by providing a method for emotion detection that is both theoretically sound and has the potential to be applied in real-world settings while presenting a mechanism for future developments in the integration of AR-based mental health care solutions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Substation Earthing System: A Finite Element Method For Minimizing Ground Resistance and Analyzing Electric Potential and Temperature Distribution
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Substation earthing systems are vital for the safety and functionality of power systems, significantly influencing their reliability. The major objectives are to reduce grounding resistance and to investigate the electric potential distribution and temperature changes within the earthing mat. This research thoroughly examines essential factors such as earthing mat dimensions, material conductivity, and soil resistivity. Utilizing visualizations like contour plots, equipotential lines, current density vectors, and temperature distribution graphs, this research enhances the understanding of earthing system behavior. The optimized design allows for rapid and efficient determination of ground resistance, thereby improving safety and operational performance in substation design.

articleTitle: Customized Machine Learning Techniques for Enhancing Cancer Detection Through Advanced Cancerous Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Early cancer identification treatment results are greatly improved by currently conventional approaches, which frequently have limitations including subjectivity and inefficiency. Several machine learning models are assessed using the Clinical and Genomic Dataset of Cancer Patients which includes both clinical and genomic characteristics, in the proposed technique. Random Forest Classifier (RFC), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), K-Means, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Decision Tree are among the techniques that have been tested. The F1 Score and Log Loss measurements are used to evaluate performance. In conclusion, SVM provides robust and accurate cancer diagnosis, making it the most dependable model for this dataset. These results highlight how machine learning can effectively use clinical and genetic data to transform early cancer detection.

articleTitle: Reliability of Electronic Connections in Fast Chargers of Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)

The driver can reduce the cost of travel both daily and over the battery's lifespan by having a previous understanding of the battery's behaviour, the grid's energy pricing, and the trip's duration.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Consumer Purchase Behaviour Analysis: Influence of Online Reviews on E-Commerce Decisions in Electronics and Electrical Markets

articleTitle: Design and Development of Chip Design for Digital Electronic System: Evolution and Trends

articleTitle: Flexible Hybrid Electronics for Printing of Nano and Chip Scale Structures

articleTitle: Natural Language Generation in AI: Developing Human-Like Text Through Deep Learning

articleTitle: Development of Hybrid Genetic Algorithm for Automated Task Planning in Multi-Satellite System

articleTitle: Feedback Control Based on Trust for Varied Automation Transparency

articleTitle: Sparse Optimization Using an MCN for Scattered Signal Suppression

abstract: In recent years, there have been reports of using deep learning to optimize the sparse array. In this context, we propose a new network that directly generates an array layout. articleTitle: Blockchain Technology and its Implications for Financial Services: A Techno-Financial Perspective

articleTitle: Scalable Performance Testing for Distributed Big Data Frameworks

abstract: The development of distributed Big Data frameworks relies heavily on performance testing because this part is what decides the robustness and scalability of systems. articleTitle: Data Analytics for Decision Support Systems in Techno-Driven Enterprises

articleTitle: Smart Water System Framework Utilizing Artificial Intelligence: Improving Water Efficiency and Crop Yield Through Data-Driven Decision-Making

articleTitle: Performance Improvement in 6G Mobile Communication Using Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The 6G mobile communication system aims to provide vast connectivity, ultra-reliable low-latency communication (URLLC), and high Information rates to support advanced applications like IoT, augmented reality, and autonomous vehicles. Traditional multiple access techniques face challenges in meeting these demands due to limitations in bandwidth efficiency and interference management. Non-orthogonal multiple Access (NOMA) offers a promising solution by allowing many users to utilize the same frequency and time resources through power domain differentiation. This paper focuses on enhancing 6G network performance by improving channel capacity, optimizing Power distribution based on user distance, and analyzing Bit error rate (BER) against Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). We employ clustering techniques to group users based on their proximity and implement adaptive power allocation strategies to maximize channel capacity, and user fairness. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of these methods, demonstrating significant improvements in spectral efficiency, channel capacity, BER vs SNR performance. Our work highlights NOMA's potential in addressing the scalability and reliability demands of dense 6G environments, paving the way for robust, high-capacity mobile communications.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning Algorithms for Early Detection of Major Depressive Disorder: A Deep Learning Approach with Twitter Data

articleTitle: Examining and Comparing: Performance of OFDM Utilised in 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: It is necessary to have a new and enhanced waveform system for transmission that is compatible with the band in order to accommodate the forthcoming 6G mobile network. Due to the fact that orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) is frequent wave form in 4Generation LTE & 5Generation new radio (NR) for enhanced mobile broadband or eMBB transmission of data on multicarrier, it is very probable that a more advanced version of OFDM will be developed for elsewhere 5G (B5G) along with the 6G mobile message scheme. In orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), several orthogonal subcarrier indicators through overlapping frequencies remain sent nearby in order to transport data simultaneously. The methods of FAST Fourier transform are the foundation upon which demodulation is built. For the purpose of altering every subcarrier (the signal) at a low symbolic rate, a conventional modulation approach, such as quadrature amplitude variation or else phase change keying, is used. As long as the bandwidth remains the same, this ensures that the overall data rates remain the same as they would be with conventional single-carrier modulation techniques. By altering the number & indexing of active subcarriers that for every OFDM subblock, a new transmission technique has been devised. This approach is capable of transmitting a greater amount of information. There is a difference between OFDM-HNIM, OFDM-SNM & OFDM-IM when compared to itself. This mixed modulation approach is superior to previous OFDM modulation systems in terms of both the spectrum & energy economy that it offers. When it comes to lower modulation rates, such as BPSK, which may deliver great dependability while still being very simple, this is particularly true. It is possible to employ this modulation approach for systems that need improved energy as well as spectrum economy, strong reliability, and minimal complexity among their requirements. In addition to flow and the greatest feasible rate, it provides a comparison regarding performance based on bit error rate (BER). For the purpose of demonstrating that the performance of the BER is consistent, Monte Carlo computations provide the evidence.

articleTitle: An Approach for the Reliability Realization of Dynamic Wireless Charging of Electric Vehicle System

articleTitle: Efficient Deep Neural Network for Intrusion Detection Using CIC-IDS-2017 Dataset
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are essential in identifying and reporting potential network attacks. IDS are classified into Host-based IDS (HIDS), which monitor internal computer threats, and Network-based IDS (NIDS), which monitor network-level attacks. IDS can also function as anomaly-based, using Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) to recognize unfamiliar attack patterns, or as rule-based, which relies on historical data-driven rules. Notably, anomaly-based IDS can detect zero-day attacks. Therefore, this study proposes a Deep Neural Network (DNN) model for anomaly-based IDS, focusing on accurate and efficient attack detection and categorization using the CIC-IDS-2017 dataset. By optimizing dataset preprocessing, the DNN architecture aims to minimize computational demands while maintaining high accuracy. Comparative evaluation with other models demonstrates the proposed model's effectiveness in attack detection despite using a simpler, more lightweight architecture than those in other studies, where more complex, less efficient approaches are often employed.

articleTitle: A Study on the Application of Artificial Intelligence in e-Justice: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The legal sector, which was earlier under-electronic, has been completely transformed by artificial intelligence (AI) with natural language processing (NLP), and it is keen to embrace digital technology for greater performance. AI's possibility of decision prognosis for non-specialists, plaintiffs, and judges can help ease case congestion problems made worse by demographic expansion. Coding systems are essential for precise textual description and subsequent activities in e-justice, which is seen as a text classification/prediction issue. These systems function differently depending on the activity and database, capturing structure, semantics, and context. It isn't easy to choose the best algorithm, utilizing several assessment measures. Numerous prediction-oriented concepts were presented to address the E-justice challenge in India. It grows difficult to detect the changing character of crimes. E-judiciary is a strategy to lower crimes and prevent illegal activity. This paper introduces the stacking-oriented E-justice prediction technique (SEJPT), which uses SVM techniques and learning-based approaches to precisely estimate crime. The SVM method outperforms other AI models, including J48, SMO Naïve Bayes Bagging, and Random Forest, in terms of domain-specific setup. The ensemble algorithm with the largest coefficient of association, which has the least mean and absolute errors, functions better than the others in some circumstances. According to the study's statistics, the suggested technique's classification accuracy was 99.6%. It is discovered that the system has a greater prediction impact than the earlier studies that used E-justice datasets as norms. The findings also show that criminological concepts may be reconciled with any experimental statistics on crime. The suggested method was also successful in forecasting potential criminal activity. Additionally, it is suggested that the stacking ensemble system's estimation accuracy surpasses that of the particular classification algorithm.

articleTitle: Understanding the Potential Advantage of Social Media Analytics for Healthcare Organizations
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)

articleTitle: An M/M/s/c Traffic Congestion Queuing Model for Toll Plazas Employed with Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: In recent time traffic congestion in the road system is a very big problem for vehicles. It is seen that many toll plazas are highly loaded with traffic and hence an appropriate analysis under queuing theory is required. At the toll plazas vehicles wait before paying the toll which causes long queues and unnecessary delays for which we develop a mathematical model for the management of traffic intensity. In this study, we analyze the system performance in the context of the parameters: average queue length, average waiting time, and total time spent in the system, and we discuss also how arrival rate, service rate, and number of servers affect queue length and waiting time. Moreover, we evaluate the lane-jockeying probability of vehicles in this study by adopting the M/M/c/c queuing model. The novelty of the study is to verify the lane-jockeying behaviors existing in the traffic system by using the ‘Levenberg-Marquardt Backpropagation’ training algorithm in ANN.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Clustering High-Dimensional Data Using K-Means
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The k-means approach is a fundamental tool in unsupervised machine learning (ML) for grouping high-dimension data. Data mining, recognizing patterns, analyzing images, bioinformatics, and ML are just a few of the fields that use clustering, an efficient quantitative data processing method. Data can be divided into categories of items with unique properties by using clustering. Numerous activities, management, and service data utilized by managers for system functional assurance are generated by cellular radio systems. Although there are strong clustering techniques like Self Organizing Mapping (SOM), there is almost no research demonstrating how well these techniques function with OAM databases that have an abundance of features (>20) gathered from real-world system adoption. Furthermore, there are still a few unresolved issues regarding the relevance of the clustering techniques. For example, when employing SOM, the beneath data fails to explicitly provide data on clusters following SOM training; therefore, the k-means method for classifying SOM components must be used afterward. In this regard, an approach for clustering radio units depending on a mix of SOM and K-means techniques is described in this study. The technique is used to identify the short-term conduct (hourly observational intervals) and long-term conduct (15 days observational duration) of wireless units by extracting cell shapes. The investigation makes use of OAM statistics gathered from a real 4G/LTE system installed in a significant European town.

articleTitle: Cloud Based Automated Control System Workshops and Rooms for Controlling Parameters
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Across all industries, cloud-based automated control systems have completely changed how operational and environmental parameters are tracked and controlled. With cloud-integrated systems for real-time data collection, processing, and control, this concept presents intelligent, remote-controlled workshops and control rooms. To guarantee accurate control of crucial variables like temperature, humidity, pressure, and equipment efficiency, these systems make use of IoT devices, AI techniques, and big data analytics. Through sophisticated data perspectives, the cloud-based strategy enables predictive maintenance, improves flexibility, and lowers operating expenses. articleTitle: Optimization of Construction Processes Using Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The rise in the Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart building construction process offers an acceptable fix to the challenging issues of energy administration, equitable expansion, and economic optimization as the number of people living in metropolitan areas rises and the desire for eco-friendly lifestyles rises. This study investigates the construction process in smart buildings by offering a deep learning (DL) approach to energy optimization. The investigation outlines a novel architecture that uses DL methods to optimize energy use in IoT-based smart buildings. To enable intelligent energy optimization and performance choices, it leverages current statistics from various resources, such as detectors, gadgets, big data processing, and smart grids. By using DL systems, such as neural networks and recurrent neural networks (RNNs), the suggested method provides accurate demand predictions while adhering to flexible use patterns. The empirical study demonstrates the efficacy of the DL-based approach using actual case investigations and intricate models conducted in multiple intelligent construction processes across the globe. Furthermore, the system's adaptability and scalability demonstrate how it may be used in a range of urban contexts. articleTitle: Dynamic Trust Management and AI-Based Multi-Factor Authentication for 6G Machine Type Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: New security concerns about the transmission of sensitive data over enormous networks of linked devices have arisen with the advent of the 6G era and the broad adoption of massive machine-type communication (MTC). The authors of this paper provide a fresh strategy for MFA and dynamic trust management in 6G networks that make use of AI to solve these issues and improve MTC security. This study presents a novel approach to behavioural profiling that takes into account the strengths and weaknesses of machine-type devices. It was necessary to create simulated data to represent many situations due to the wide range of possible network circumstances, device characteristics, ambient variables, applications load of work, and security needs. The efficacy of the suggested remedy was evaluated during six simulation cycles. The findings showed that the framework can adapt to changing network circumstances and device behaviours, with stability demonstrated across many situations. The accuracy rates for implementing MFA ranged from 0.49 to 0.57. This MFA and AI-driven dynamic trust management framework has great potential to improve 6G network MTC security; its adaptability and resilience provide a solid basis for meeting the security concerns that will inevitably arise in the future of 6G networks. To maximize performance and assure successful deployment, more modifications and real-life testing are suggested.

articleTitle: Recommender Systems in E-Commerce: A Deep Dive into AI-Driven Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: In e-commerce, recommender systems are the most widely used systems that satisfy the user with personalized recommendations, and they have a significant influence on e-business success. In the new era of artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning techniques, modern recommender systems have evolved from the classical models of content-based filtration systems to highly sophisticated and accurate models. In this post, we take a closer look at specific optimization techniques that are applied in the context of AI-based recommender systems in the e-commerce industry. We start with the data needed to train these systems and the different ways to collect and clean the data. Next, we delve into getting recommendations and the methods behind them - collaborative filtering (CF), content-based filtering (CB), etc. Next, we explain how deep learning approaches such as natural language processing and neural networks improve the accuracy of these systems. We look at what sort of problems you face while implementing these systems (cold-start issue, data sparsity issues et al) and how are you working to address them. We also consider ethical concerns regarding recommender systems: bias and privacy. Finally, we summarize the various use cases of AI-based recommender systems in e-commerce, including product recommendations, personalized promotions, and user profiling. This paper intends to present a general survey of the techniques which are being state-of-the-art in e-commerce AI recommender systems and a brief discussion of how they can massively boost user satisfaction in unison with business goals.

articleTitle: Risk Management Model in Electronic Banking Using Machine Learning Based Fraud Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Risk management techniques have been used for a long time, they are just now becoming well-known in the electronic banking industry. At this stage, risk management is essential to the entire operations of financial institutions. Financial institutions must evaluate the procedures that support their business functions against prospective risks, weaknesses, and possible effects to determine the degree of risk exposures and any lingering dangers. Additionally, high financial processing expenses are necessary due to the notable rise in fraud in e-banking. Consequently, fraud detection in e-banking has emerged as an intriguing subject for risk management. The application of category weight-tuning parameters to regulate the value of authentic and fraud transactions is examined in this paper. By considering the voting procedure, this study suggests using weight-tuning as a pre-process for imbalanced datasets in addition to Cat-Boost and XG-Boost to enhance the Light-GBM technique's efficiency. Lastly, this study employs deep learning to adjust the hyperparameters, especially the suggested weight-tuning to significantly enhance efficiency. This study employs recall-precision measurements to the conventional ROC-AUC to more effectively handle unbalanced databases. A five-fold cross-validating technique is used for assessing Cat-Boost, Light-GBM, and XG-Boost independently. Additionally, the efficiency of the paired methods is evaluated using the predominant vote ensemble learning technique. The outcomes show that Light-GBM and XG-Boost meet the optimal degree criterion of ROC-AUC = 0.952, precision 0.79, recall 0.80, Fl-value 0.79, and MCC 0.79. When compared to the state-of-the-art techniques, this is a major advance.

articleTitle: MRAM-Based Physical Unclonable Function that is Resilient to Deep Learning Attacks
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Electronic devices are everywhere, so strong hardware security is needed to keep private data safe from dangers. A physical Unclonable Function (PUF) device constructed using magneto-resistive random-access memory (MRAM) is shown in this study. The circuit generates appropriate outputs for problem-solving by using built-in properties derived from various manufacturing processes, such as the resistance of the magnetic tunnel junction (MTJ) cell. This proposal differs from Arbiter PUF in that it satisfies the rigorous avalanche criteria (SAC). Additionally, the proposed circuit is impervious to machine learning-based modelling assaults due to its grid-like architecture. Various ML approaches are evaluated for two- and four-array designs, including systems such as support vector machine (SVM), linear regression (LR), and multilayer perceptron (MLP). Accuracy of MLP-attack forecasts remained 53.62% for two array circuit & 49.88% for four array circuit. This demonstrates that the system continues to function well despite substantial process modifications. A convolutional neural network (CNN), a recurrent neural network (RNN), a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), and a Larq are all used in high-dimensional models that are based on deep learning. These nets have an accuracy rating of 50.32%, 50.26%, and 50.32%, along with 50.32%, correspondingly. For a simpler two-array design, the suggested circuit's efficiency at the layout stage is also looked into. Based on the simulations, the suggested circuit has an average intra-hamming distance (HD) of 0.99% and an average inter-hamming distance (HD) of 49.97%. It also has an average diffuseness of 49.08.

articleTitle: Statistical Load Forecasting in Power Systems: A Comparative Study of SARIMA and Prophet Models
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Load forecasting is essential for effective energy management and planning in power systems. This study compares the Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA) and Prophet models for predicting hourly electricity consumption data from PJM Interconnection LLC. The primary objective is to identify the best-performing model between the two. The results reveal key insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each model, providing valuable guidance for their application in various load-prediction scenarios. The findings aim to improve the accuracy and reliability of statistical forecasting methods in energy management.

articleTitle: Advancements in Additive Manufacturing: Optimizing Mechanical Properties Through AI-Based Design
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: Modern engineering has been transformed by additive manufacturing (AM), which makes complicated geometries and customized constructions possible. Nonetheless, there are so many interconnected variables that optimising mechanical properties is still difficult. To improve mechanical performance in AM, this work investigates AI-driven design optimization strategies. Tensile strength, material toughness, and weight reduction efficiency are predicted by utilizing machine learning models to analyze critical aspects like layer height, print speed, infill density, and extrusion temperature. Metrics like MSE, MAE, and R2 scores are used to compare the predictive accuracy of various AI models, such as neural networks, random forests, and support vector machines. The findings show that while using less material, AI-based optimization greatly increases structural integrity. The connections between print parameters and performance results are shown graphically. This study demonstrates how AI may simplify AM procedures, opening the door to more intelligent, high-performance manufacturing systems with improved productivity and material use.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality for Enhanced Surgical Precision: A Framework for Real-Time Visualization and Navigation
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The advancement of Augmented reality (AR) technology has made it possible to use it in surgical precision and better the lives of patients. This paper outlines a real-time visualization and navigation framework where AR is integrated into surgical work. CT and MRI imaging data are used in the system to create accurate and rather detailed preoperative 3D anatomical models. These models are overlaid on the surgeon's vision, being the integral part of the system, providing the surgeon with dynamic constant assistance during procedures. To surmount the problem of misalignment of the virtual overlays with the patient's anatomy due to movements of the patient in the operating room, the framework uses complex tracking algorithms as well as machine learning techniques. It highlights planner pre-operative, intra-operative visualization and decision support mainly in complicated surgical cases. In the case of minimally invasive surgery, the framework was used to position the instruments correctly with improved accuracy, cutting short on time to operate, and countering complications. This research shows how AR can benefit today's surgery, as an origination of increased accuracy and a closing of the gap between conception and operations. It has also discussed some of the issues like scalability, cost, and the required training for the surgeon for the use of such system and has therefore provided a direction for the large-scale use of AR-assisted surgical systems.

articleTitle: AI Driven Transformation: Updated Technologies in 6G Communication System
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)

articleTitle: Design Process and Development of Automation for Smart Buildings

articleTitle: Event-Driven Architectures for Real-Time Analytics in Big Data Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 First International Conference on Advances in Computer Science, Electrical, Electronics, and Communication Technologies (CE2CT)
abstract: The buzzword in big data processing is Event-Driven Architecture (EDA), which is proving to be an effective alternative to processing data in real-time. As we know, the traditional batch processing methods are not enough to meet the demand for real-time analytics owing to the exponential growth of Big Data. Event-driven architecture provides a loosely coupled and scalable implementation, as it decouples the components of a system, where data flows between them asynchronously in response to events. We have built upon the principles of EDA and its applications in the domain of real-time analytics for Big Data. There are three moving parts to an EDA: an event producer, an event broker, and an event consumer. On the event producer, you will create events according to when the data changes in data or drive an event based on the user acting; it gets saved into the event broker. The consumer then consumes this data, processes events and produces insights in real-time. EDA has several benefits for big data systems. It is able to process large amounts of data simultaneously in real-time to facilitate timely decision-making for organizations. It has fault tolerance and horizontal scalability so that it can handle spikes well. It also offers greater ease of processing events and improved integration with diverse data sources. Pervasive phenomenon of Big Data: with, EDA is emerging as a viable contender in real-time analytics processing.

articleTitle: Reimagining Mythology with Virtual Reality: Postmodernist Techniques for Immersive Retellings in Educational Platforms

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Efficiency in IoT inside Smart Grids Utilizing Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence Techniques

articleTitle: Enhancing Ground Network in UAV Assisted Wireless Communication

abstract: The development of wireless technology for ground communications is being aided by the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs).
